articles.title: Golden State Warriors vs. Los Angeles Lakers Live NBA Updates, Scores and Highlights
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Lakers made a statement Wedneday night to open the 2026-27 NBA regular season, throttling the Golden State Warriors 127-105.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Lakers made a statement Wedneday night to open the 2026-27 NBA regular season, throttling the Golden State Warriors 127-105.

Luka Dončić did his usual amount of stat-stuffing, finishing with 28 points, eight rebounds, seven assists and a team-best plus-31. After a slow start by his standards, Austin Reaves ended up pumping out 25 points and 6 assists.

But it was Walker Kessler who stole the show. Making his Lakers regular-season debut, he dropped 24 points on a perfect 12-of-12 shooting. Ten of these makes were dunks. You're reading all of that correctly.

Stephen Curry churned out 23 points on 7-of-15 shooting but was just 2-of-7 from three and did most of his damage in the first quarter. Yaxel Lendeborg was solid in his rookie-year debut for someone who spent so much time defending Luka. He was also trolled by Dončić and the rest of the Lakers roster. Silver linings end here for the Dubs.

Scroll on for all the highlights, analysis and takeaways from this lopsided clash that you can handle.

I will pay obscene amounts of I.O.U. cryptocurrency to anyone who can procure the hot mics for this exchange. The world needs to know what Yaxel said.

At long last, the second half that wouldn't end is officially over. The Lakers annihilated the Warriors after the first quarter, outscoring them by a total of 33 points in the second and third frames combined.

L.A. can feel good coming out of this one. Walker Kessler won't always make every shot, but their defensive aggression and depth shined.

The Warriors, on the other hand, have some existential questions to ask themselves. Chief among them: Just what the hell are they doing here?

Sure, this take from The Athletic's Nick Friedell is one way to look at it. But who's to say Steve Kerr wasn't forcing his players to mull over the giant goose egg they just laid a little bit longer by prolonging the game?

Lots of basketball is left to play. This season. Not in this game. This game is over .

Anyway, we shouldn't rush to judgment after a single win. At the very least, though, we can say the trio of Luka, Reaves and Kessler has a chance to be special—if not dominant. The synergy between them is already off the charts, and there's still 81 games left to play.

Score: Lakers 120, Warriors 96 | 3:05 remaining in the fourth quarter

Walker Kessler Went Full Wilt in his Lakers Debut

Even with most of these looks coming as dunks, this is just ridiculous.

Elsewhere, Jake LaRavia badly rolled his ankle and didn't immediately get off the floor. The Lakers have subbed him out of the game.

Score: Lakers 116, Warriors 83 |5:34 remaining in the fourth quarter

So much for shortening that rotation, right?

No word yet on whether Steve Kerr will allow Draymond Green to leave the bench and set up his podcast equipment in the locker room.

The Warriors also sorta stink. But the Lakers' bench does run deeper than last season, when the reserves ranked 14th in point differential per 100 possessions.

From being able to move Sandro Mamukelashvili to the center spot to bringing Quentin Grimes off the pine to take on more ball-handling when Collin Sexton is unavailable, this roster just has more optionality.

That doesn't mean every game will be like this . But it's a pretty good harbinger for surviving the season.

Score: Lakers 111, Warriors 83 | 11:00 remaining in the fourth quarter

In addition to the pain Walker Kessler is inflicting around the basket, the Lakers as a team are shooting 27-of-32 on shots within five feet of the hoop. That's a tidy 84 percent clip.

Score: Lakers 102, Warriors 70 | 11:27 remaining in the fourth quarter

The Lakers Weren't Kidding About Playing Aggressive Defense

On top of forcing the Warriors into 14 total turnovers, the Lakers have seven pick-sixes that they've turned into 19 points. Head coach JJ Redick was serious when he said this team would get after it on the less-glamorous end.

We'd nevertheless be remiss if we declared this Los Angeles' new normal. The Warriors a caricature of a basketball team right now. We need to see how the Lakers' defense holds up against a roster with actual hope for this season.

Walker Kessler Already Making Lakers History

So, um, maybe the Lakers actually underpaid for Walker Kessler?

Score: Lakers 87, Warriors 61 | 4:45 remaining in the third quarter

Walker Kessler is 10-of-10 from the floor, with nine of those shots coming as dunks

Steve Kerr has more rage timeouts (two) than Draymond Green has made shots (one)

Stephen Curry has missed his last five field-goal attempts

The Lakers have a 210 offensive rating in transition

Score: Lakers 78, Warriors 57 | 8:03 remaining in the third quarter

The Lakers are Obliterating the Warriors in Transition

Somebody needs to check on Steve Kerr as we start the third quarter.

The rookie has the entire Lakers bench giving him crap. I'm actually dying.

What a way to make your NBA regular-season debut.

Suffice it to say, the folks at Crypto.com Arena don't seem to be missing LeBron very much.

Luka Hits a Buzzer-Beater from Half-Court 😳

Dončić is showing no mercy to the Dubs' rookie. At all.

Luka is up to 23 points, six rebounds and four assists on the evening. Walker Kessler still hasn't missed. The Lakers' defense held Golden state to just 19 points in the second quarter.

Warriors not named Stephen Curry are shooting 13-of-35 from the floor. Golden State has also allowed the Lakers to shoot 84 percent (16-of-19) around the basket, according to Prime Stats .

Score: Lakers 66, Warriors 52 | HALFTIME

Walker Kessler is up to 6-of-6 shooting from the floor. It turns out playing with Luka Dončić is good.

Score: Lakers 63, Warriors 52 | 22.4 seconds remaining in the second quarter

Yaxel Lendeborg is defending Luka a bunch tonight, and Luka isn't taking it easy on him.

You have to love this energy if you're the Dubs. Heck, even Dončić seems to appreciate it.

In other news, the Lakers are on an 8-0 run and threatening to open the lead heading into halftime. The Warriors' transition and rim defense is suboptimal. Steve Kerr's body language is shimmying between apoplectic and total resignation.

Score: Lakers 58, Warriors 50 | 1:12 remaining in the second quarter

What a catch-and-finish by Jake LaRavia. He looks good to open the year—a lot more comfortable from beyond the arc, too.

Luka owes him dinner for turning this into an assist, by the way.

Score: Lakers 53, Warriors 48 | 2:28 remaining in the second quarter

Golden State is getting rocked in transition right now. Three of the Dubs' five turnovers have turned into pick-sixes.

Steve Kerr isn't happy. While it's tough to blame him, he should take a good look at the roster. This might be a common occurrence all year.

Score: Lakers 45, Warriors 41 | 7:17 remaining in the second quarter

This is a Big Deal If the Warriors Keep It Up

The Dubs wound up finishing minus-one without Curry in the first. But considering those lineups are headlined by the likes of Brandon Williams, Gui Santos, Al Horford, Will Richard and rookie Yaxel Lendeborg, they'll surely take it.

Score: Lakers 34, Warriors 33 | Start of the second quarter

Steph already has 16 points. Luka tallied 13 to go along with three assists. We had 10 lead changes. And 10 ties. Both teams have offensive ratings north of 130. Brandon Williams got all the way to the basket in the half-court, something Golden State isn't used to seeing.

We could be in for some fireworks, folks.

Score: Lakers 34, Warriors 33 | End of the first quarter

Golden State subbed out Steph after he dropped 16 points in under eight minutes. He looks spry for someone who pulled up lame in an open practice and sent everyone into a social media tizzy just a few days ago.

Score: Warriors 27, Lakers 26 | 2:50 remaining in the first quarter

We've been watching stuff like this for almost 15 years. Anybody else feel old?

Score: Warriors 24, Lakers 24 | 3:40 remaining in the first quarter

First Luka-Kessler Alley-Oop of the Season

We need a name for this Luka Dončić-Walker Kessler connection. I have no good ideas. My bad idea: Luka SkyWalker.

Please send all your suggestions my way.

The first of many threes for Chef Curry.

Proof: He already has two on the evening

Score: Warriors 13, Lakers 10 | 7:23 remaining in the first quarter

Yaxel Lendeborg's First Career NBA Points

The Golden State Warriors' rookie is on the board—off an assist from Steph no less!

Relatedly, Steph, Luka Dončić, Yaxel Lendeborg and Walker Kessler all scored within the first 90 seconds. A social media admin's fever dream.

Score: Warriors 10, Lakers 10 | 7:41 remaining in the first quarter

I'm not sure whether Stephen Curry's circus shots are a better pregame tradition than LeBron James' chalk toss. I'm just glad we have both. Still.

The Kristaps Porziņģis Trade Destination Is...

We've got a little time to kill before opening tip, so let's go here. The answer is the Milwaukee Bucks .

Trading Giannis Antetokounmpo has thrust them into a bigger-picture focus. And since they don't control their own first-round pick again until 2030, they needn't be overly focused on rostering players who will actually, you know, play.

Landing Porziņģis is also a way for the Bucks to offload the three years and $81.6 million left on Myles Turner's deal. The trade:

Golden State Warriors Receive: Myles Turner

Milwaukee Bucks Receive: Moses Moody and Kristaps Porziņģis

Sending Turner out in exchange for KP and Moody works financially and gives the Bucks more palatable numbers with which to work. Porziņģis is guaranteed just $3 million in 2027-28 while Moody, including this season, has two years and $25.9 million left on his contract.

Whether the Warriors bite is a separate matter. Having Turner on the books for next season torpedoes their cap-space plans. But star players don't leave in free agency anymore.

If Golden State is holding out hope for Nikola Jokić (player option), Giannis Antetokounmpo (player option), Karl-Anthony Towns (player option) or someone it'll have to strike a trade anyway. Turner's salary would prove to be valuable matching fodder in those scenarios. In the interim, he provides the Warriors with a floor-spacer and rim protector at the 5 who they can sell to the fanbase as (feeble) proof that they're not letting what's left of Stephen Curry go out sadly.

Lakers and Warriors Make Starting 5s Official

Stephen Curry, Yaxel Lendeborg and Draymond Green always figured to be in the starting five. De'Anthony Melton and Gui Santos getting the nod are direct result of absences from Brandin Podziemski and Kristaps Porziņģis.

My guess is Melton will head back to the bench once Podz returns. With that said, Santos may join him if Steve Kerr thinks it's wiser to start Al Horford—something he probably can't even think about until Charles Bassey (knee) or the Dubs trade for another big.

For the Lakers, this is about as expected. Quentin Grimes profiles as a starter over Matisse Thybulle moving forward, but Collin Sexton's absence leaves a backcourt void on the bench.

It isn't only the Warriors dealing with a bunch of absences on Wednesday night. The Lakers will be without rookie Cameron Carr (oblique), Adou Thiero (knee) and Collin Sexton (calf). At least two of those three are expected to be rotation regulars, which is why JJ Redick already seems to be tightening the belt.

This should have the biggest impact on the wing and guard ranks. With Sexton out in particular, it feels like Austin Reaves or Luka Dončić will end up hitting the 40-minute threshold—provided we're not headed for a blowout.

ESPN's Shams Charania reported earlier today that the Golden State Warriors are exploring trades for Kristaps Porziņģis, who is apparently considering walking away from basketball as he deals with lingering effects from his postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome (POTS).

Shortly thereafter, The Athletic's Sam Amick and Nick Friedell confirmed that the Dubs have held discussions with the Milwaukee Bucks about a potential deal.

Porziņģis is making $20 million this year and is guaranteed just $3 million next season, making him a quasi-expiring contract. It isn't clear what Golden State wants in return, or how aggressively it's willing to sweeten a package knowing that Jimmy Butler and Moses Moody won't be playing anytime soon.

This whole situation is insane—right down to the Warriors seemingly having little knowledge on the state of Porziņģis' health.

articles.title: Giannis Gets MVP Chants From Fans Less Than 2 Minutes Into Heat Debut in Trending Video
articles.summary: Giannis Antetokounmpo received a warm welcome from the crowd at Kaseya Center as he made his Miami Heat debut on Wednesday night.
articles.body:
Giannis Antetokounmpo received a warm welcome from the crowd at Kaseya Center as he made his Miami Heat debut on Wednesday night.

Fans chanted "MVP" at Antetokounmpo while he attempted free throws with just over 10 minutes remaining in the first quarter of Miami's matchup with the Minnesota Timberwolves.

The Heat acquired the two-time MVP as part of a blockbuster trade with the Milwaukee Bucks on June 22.

Miami received Antetokounmpo and Bobby Portis from Milwaukee in exchange for Tyler Herro, Kel'el Ware, Jaime Jaquez Jr., Kasparas Jakucionis, three first-round draft picks, one pick swap and one second-round pick.

Antetokounmpo made a strong first impression on Wednesday, scoring 14 points and grabbing two rebounds during the first quarter. He also shot 5-of-6 from the field in the opening period.

The 31-year-old was pleased with Miami's progress in training camp heading into its season opener.

"I think our chemistry is where it should be," Antetokounmpo said Tuesday, per Anthony Chiang of the Miami Herald . "Our approach is incredible. I think we've worked extremely hard these 22 days that we've been in training camp. We've gotten together as a team. We've done a lot of activities off the court as a team. Not only do we spend time here, we spend time out of here.

"So I think our mindset is exactly where it should be. Obviously, we're going to get better. This is Game 1. In Game 40, we're going to be a better team as long as everybody is healthy and everybody is available. So we just got to keep on taking it one step at a time. But the first step, which was training camp, we attacked that step very, very well. I'm proud of myself. I'm proud of the team. Hopefully, we can go out there and show it."

While the Heat missed the playoffs with a record of 43-39 last season, expectations are high following the addition of Antetokounmpo.

He's coming off a stellar 13-year tenure with Milwaukee in which he amassed 10 All-Star nods, nine All-NBA selections, one Defensive Player of the Year award, one championship and a Finals MVP honor.

Antetokounmpo also left the Bucks as their all-time leading scorer .

As he begins the next chapter of his career, he's already receiving plenty of support from Heat fans.

articles.title: What did Paul George do? NBA fines Celtics star $2,000 after record-breaking debut
articles.summary: Paul George has been fined $2,000 by the NBA for flopping in his Celtics debut.
articles.body: Paul George has been fined $2,000 by the NBA for flopping in his Celtics debut. The league announced the penalty Wednesday, a day after Boston’s 121-113 season-opening loss in Detroit. One play with about three minutes left drew the review, and it was only one piece of a busy first night. The nine-time All-Star also scored more points than any Celtic has in a debut, while Boston gave away a 22-point lead. Here is what the league saw on that play, and what else George did in about 31 minutes.Why did the NBA fine Paul George $2,000?As there were about three minutes left in regulation, George ran in transition and bumped Duncan Robinson. The contact was light. George went down hard anyway, and the league office ruled the fall a flop. The NBA posted the result on X on Wednesday, October 21, saying George was “assessed a postgame Flopping fine of $2,000 upon league office review.” The announcement came less than 24 hours after the final buzzer.The rulebook treats flops two ways. One called during play costs the offender a technical foul and gives the other team a free throw. One found afterward, like this one, brings a fine, and the amounts rise for repeat offenders. No suspension comes with it, so George is free to play Friday.Robinson, the player George ran into, had a good night himself. He scored 21 for the Pistons, 15 of them in the fourth quarter, when Detroit ran off 23 straight points to take over the game. Cade Cunningham and Jalen Duren added 22 points apiece.Paul George breaks the Celtics’ debut recordGeorge scored 38 points in about 31 minutes, topping the 30 Kristaps Porzingis put up in his own Celtics debut. The line also had five rebounds, three assists and five steals. George made 12 of 21 shots and went 7 for 8 at the line. Only five other players in NBA history have matched 38 points, five rebounds, five steals and seven threes in a single game. George also passed Kyle Korver on the all-time three-point list.The three-point work stands out. Seven makes on 12 tries is 58 percent, well above last season’s 39.2 percent mark, when George averaged 17.3 points. George was drafted by the Pacers in 2010, so this is season 16.Boston acquired George over the summer from Philadelphia in exchange for Jaylen Brown. George is also a co-captain with Jayson Tatum, who had a rough opener. Tatum made six of 23 shots and missed all seven threes, though he handed out 11 assists.The Celtics led by as many as 22 and lost anyway. articles.title: Atlanta Dream and Golden State Valkyries skip national anthem for third straight WNBA Finals game
articles.summary: Atlanta Dream and Golden State Valkyries skipped the national anthem for a third straight WNBA Finals game despite the league's own rulebook mandate.
articles.body: ATLANTA – A change of cities did not bring a change in the Atlanta Dream and Golden State Valkyries’ national anthem routine. Both teams were off the court during the anthem before Game 3 of the WNBA Finals on Wednesday night at State Farm Arena, marking their third straight absence despite a provision in the league’s own rulebook calling for players to stand and line up during the performance. Just like in Games 1 and 2, players jogged off the court just seconds before the start of the anthem and returned mere moments after it concluded. DREAM, VALKYRIES SKIP NATIONAL ANTHEM IN WNBA FINALS GAME 2 DESPITE RULEBOOK REQUIREMENT The WNBA, both teams and the NBA still have not answered OutKick’s questions about the absences. WNBA rulebook calls for players to stand and line up The WNBA’s 2026 official rulebook says players, coaches and trainers are to "stand and line up in a dignified posture" along the sidelines or on the foul line during the national anthem. OutKick asked the WNBA whether any discipline was planned or under consideration following the anthem absences, whether either team had received an exemption and whether the league would instruct the teams to be on the court for Game 3. Both teams were asked to explain their absences and whether the league had communicated any instructions or expectations about the anthem. OutKick first contacted the WNBA, Dream and Valkyries after Saturday’s opener, followed up Sunday and contacted all three again Tuesday. NBA also received questions before Game 3 The questions extended to the NBA league office before the series moved to Atlanta. OutKick contacted NBA Executive Vice President and Chief Communications Officer Mike Bass on Tuesday, asking whether the NBA has any role in overseeing or enforcing the WNBA’s anthem provision. NBA STAYS SILENT ON WNBA FINALS TEAMS SKIPPING NATIONAL ANTHEM IN GAMES 1 AND 2 The inquiry also asked whether NBA Commissioner Adam Silver or anyone at the NBA league office had discussed the absences with WNBA leadership, whether any guidance had been provided and whether the teams would be instructed to be present for Wednesday’s anthem. The NBA did not respond. OutKick also sought to ask about the anthem during the Finals press conferences. I raised my hand at all five of Saturday’s pregame and postgame sessions, all four coaches’ sessions Monday and both coaches’ pregame sessions Wednesday, but was not called on in any of the 11. VANCE CONDEMNS 'DISGRACEFUL' WNBA NATIONAL ANTHEM WALKOUTS, SAYS PLAYERS SHOULD SHOW MORE GRATITUDE The teams weren’t the only ones who didn’t stand for Wednesday’s anthem. Two people seated in an area designated for WNBA public relations staff remained in their seats during the performance. Afterward, I asked both why they hadn’t stood. Neither provided an explanation. OutKick could not immediately confirm their identities and is working to determine their names and roles. The venue changed, but the anthem absences continued. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Three games into the Finals, the WNBA’s own rulebook calls for a lineup, its teams remain off the floor and the league still has not explained the apparent violation.

articles.title: Anthony Edwards' historic performance ruins Giannis Antetokounmpo's Miami debut as Timberwolves blow out Heat
articles.summary: Edwards put on a scoring clinic, becoming the third player in NBA history to have multiple 40-point season openers.
articles.body:
The Giannis Antetokounmpo era with the Miami Heat has begun with a loss.

In his first game with his new team after being traded from the Bucks in the offseason, Antetokounmpo and the Heat opened the season with a 131-106 blowout loss to the Minnesota Timberwolves.

Miami's problem in the loss wasn't its new forward. He finished with a team-high 35 points, six rebounds and an assist.

The problem was the nonexistent backcourt defense. The Heat had no answer for Anthony Edwards, who finished with 45 points, and his backcourt mate, LaMelo Ball, who had 21.

Edwards made league history in the dominant win. The Minnesota guard became just the third player in NBA history to have multiple 40-point season openers, joining Wilt Chamberlain (4) and Michael Jordan (3). Edwards had 41 in Minnesota's season-opening win against the Portland Trail Blazers last year.

Edwards and Ball dominated from beyond the arc, hitting 14 of 30 combined attempts, while Miami, as a team, made just 8 of 33. Edwards' nine 3-pointers set a franchise record for a Minnesota season opener.

Antetokounmpo somehow went from half court to a dunk without the ball touching the ground.

Antetokounmpo made sure to show off the handles against Rudy Gobert.

While Antetokounmpo has a height advantage over Edwards, the two had a fun second-quarter sequence: the guard drained a 3, and the Heat forward followed with an emphatic dunk, accompanied by some trash talk.

Antetokounmpo and Edwards each had 21 points in the first half.

Edwards spent most of the game giving the Heat a piece of his mind, and he backed up his talk with his performance.

Antetokounmpo began his career with the Milwaukee Bucks, who selected him with the 15th overall pick in the 2013 NBA Draft. After 13 seasons in Milwaukee, including an NBA championship in 2021, the two-time MVP and the Bucks disagreed over his future, and he requested a trade.

Antetokounmpo finally got the trade he wanted this past summer as the Milwaukee Bucks sent him and Bobby Portis to Miami for Tyler Herro, Kel'el Ware, Jaime Jaquez Jr., Kasparas Jakučionis and five draft picks.

The Heat return to action Friday, looking to notch their first win of the season against the Detroit Pistons.

Meanwhile, Minnesota will stay in Florida and take on the Orlando Magic on Friday.

articles.title: Kawhi Spoils Caleb Wilson's Debut, Box Score Player Stats & Highlights from Bulls vs. Raptors
articles.summary: Kawhi Leonard's return to Toronto couldn't have gone any better as the Raptors took down the visiting Chicago Bulls 135-92 on Wednesday evening in both teams' 2026-27 regular season debuts.
articles.body:
Kawhi Leonard's return to Toronto couldn't have gone any better as the Raptors took down the visiting Chicago Bulls 135-92 on Wednesday evening in both teams' 2026-27 regular season debuts.

Here's a look at notable box score stats for Toronto, which was a 9.5-point favorite, per FanDuel Sportsbook .

The Raptors led 43-23 after the first quarter, 69-44 at halftime and 103-71 after the third quarter. Toronto kept its foot on the gas, though, and outscored Chicago 32-21 in the fourth.

Toronto acquired Leonard, who led Toronto to its lone NBA championship in 2019 before leaving in free agency for the Los Angeles Clippers, back from L.A. via trade this summer. So far, so good for Leonard's return, as he might be the missing piece Toronto needs to make a deep playoff run.

The quartet of Leonard, Scottie Barnes, Immanuel Quickley and RJ Barrett combined for 89 points, 20 rebounds, 17 assists and six steals despite playing an average of 26 minutes. Quickley ended up finishing plus-38.

Chicago is a young and rebuilding team that will have better basketball waiting someday. However, this was a very difficult opening game for head coach Tiago Splitter's group.

Here's a look at Chicago's top four scorers, including rookie forward Caleb Wilson, the No. 4 overall pick in the draft.

The Bulls committed 27 turnovers and shot just 4-of-36 from three (11 percent). Overall, Chicago made only 32 percent of its field goals. Josh Giddey had three more turnovers (five) than points (two) and shot just 1-of-10.

Bulls rookie forward Caleb Wilson had a tough debut, committing nine turnovers (no assists). The Raptors outscored the Bulls by 45 points with him on the floor. Wilson also shot just 7-of-21 and made only 1-of-8 threes.

There were a few bright spots. For starters, Wilson amassed three steals and a block, and he showcased the offensive talents that can make him a star someday.

Both teams will play road games on Friday. Toronto will visit the Washington Wizards, and Chicago will take on the Milwaukee Bucks. Washington beat Milwaukee 128-116 on Wednesday behind a 34-point, 12-rebound effort from big man Anthony Davis.

articles.title: Sergio de Larrea da sus primeros pasos en la NBA rodeado de estrellas
articles.standfirst: El base español hace su debut con los Dallas Mavericks en el regreso de Kyrie Irivng frente a los Rockets de Kevin Durant
articles.summary: El base español hace su debut con los Dallas Mavericks en el regreso de Kyrie Irivng frente a los Rockets de Kevin Durant
articles.body: Después de verse las caras dos veces en la preparación, los Mavericks y los Rockets abrían su temporada en el Toyota Center de Houston, en un partido que ya es histórico para Sergio de Larrea tras producirse su debut oficial en la NBA y convertirse en el vigesimoprimer español en conseguirlo. El partido no tuvo color y se decidió bastante rápido. Tras un primer cuarto igualado, el 12-38 del segundo cuarto sentenció el encuentro para los Rockets, que se divirtieron a través de Durant (30 puntos), Jabari Smith Jr. (30) y Sengun (23). Por parte de los Mavericks, Cooper Flagg anotó 32 puntos y Kyrie Irving, en su esperado regreso tras 597 días de ausencia por lesión, sumó 15 puntos. El jugador de Valladolid apenas tuvo que esperar unos minutos para saltar a la pista. A falta de 4:08 para finalizar el primer cuarto, 'Larry' se estrenó con los Dallas Mavericks, aunque su primera rotación fue corta. No obstante, le dio tiempo a realizar su primera acción positiva: un rebote ofensivo que derivó en la jugada polémica del partido; la expulsión de Tari Eason por un empujón sobre P.J. Washington. Cuando quedaban 2:45, el base volvió al banquillo. En el segundo cuarto, de Larrea entró a pista quedando 8:37 para el descanso en unos Mavs desordenados que ya perdían por más de diez puntos. Con 6:17 para el final del periodo, el base consiguió su primera asistencia en la liga con un pase picado para el tiro flotante de Naji Marshall, poco después de fallar su primer triple intentado. El vallisoletano no volvió a pisar el parquet hasta el 1:49 para el final del partido, en los que apenas pudo coger su segundo rebote del partido. Ahora sólo falta esperar para verle con más minutos y seguir evolucionando como jugador. Ayer fue el turno de Mara, hoy le tocó a de Larrea, el siguiente será Miller. El futuro ya está aquí.

articles.title: Jordan Clarkson's 10,106-square-foot Texas mansion hits the market for $7.5 million in 2026 with a private basketball court and cinema
articles.summary: Jordan Clarkson’s San Antonio mansion is back on the market, and the $7.5 million listing comes with several features built for life beyond the basketball
articles.body: Jordan Clarkson’s San Antonio mansion is back on the market, and the $7.5 million listing comes with several features built for life beyond the basketball court. The three-storey property covers 10,106 square feet in The Dominion, a gated community in his hometown.It has a private half basketball court, a cinema with stadium-style seating, an infinity-edge pool and a detached guesthouse with a full bar. Clarkson acquired the house in January 2023 through JClarkson Enterprises LLC.Jordan Clarkson's mansion has a private basketball court, cinema and four-car garageThe estate stands on a 1.12-acre lot at Crescent Park in The Dominion. Built in 2008, the Mediterranean-style property has five bedrooms, six full bathrooms and one half-bathroom. The listing describes a home designed for entertaining, with dedicated spaces for recreation, dining and relaxation.The half basketball court is one of its defining features. Clarkson can shoot at home without leaving the property, while the indoor theater offers stadium-style seating and a hardwood concession counter. A separate game room gives the house another entertainment area, and a wine lounge provides a dedicated space for drinks and hosting guests. The property also has an elevator connecting its levels.The main bedroom is among the home's largest rooms. Realtor.com lists its dimensions as 24 by 16 feet and notes that it has outdoor access, a sitting area and a walk-in closet. Its bathroom measures 15 by 18 feet and has separate vanities and a separate tub and shower. These details give prospective buyers a clearer idea of how the estate is laid out beyond its overall square footage.The kitchen has professional-grade appliances, custom cabinetry and an island. The listing also identifies a separate dining room, an eat-in kitchen, a breakfast bar and a walk-in pantry. Three or more fireplaces are listed among the home's features, including wood-burning and gas options.The outdoor amenities extend beyond the basketball court. The property has a private swimming pool with an infinity edge, a spa and an Italian wood-burning pizza oven. A stainless-steel Viking gas grill is also mentioned in the earlier property report. The detached casita gives visitors a separate place to stay, with its own bathroom, sitting area and full bar. Its lower level includes a gym and a full bathroom.There is also an attached garage with space for at least four cars, plus additional storage. Realtor.com lists mature trees, landscaped grounds and views of the city and a bluff among the property's features. The Dominion community itself lists controlled and guarded access, a golf course, tennis facilities, a clubhouse, parks and jogging trails among its amenities. Why Jordan Clarkson's San Antonio mansion is listed for $7.5 millionThe property's price has a history. Texas attorney Thomas J. Henry owned the estate before selling it in January 2023. He had listed the home for $7.5 million, the same asking price Clarkson's property now carries. The San Antonio Express-News reported at the time that public records linked the buyer, JClarkson Enterprises LLC, to Clarkson. The final sale price was not disclosed.One figure from that transaction should not be mistaken for the purchase price. According to the Express-News, JClarkson Enterprises LLC borrowed $3.78 million from City National Bank for the acquisition. That was the reported loan amount, not confirmation of what Clarkson paid for the house. The public reporting does not establish the final purchase price, so it is not possible to calculate his profit or loss from the current listing.The present listing identifies Janay Bankston of Barlowe Daly Realty as the listing agent. Realtor.com showed the property at $7.5 million and listed a homeowners association fee of $295 per month. Its listing also gave an annual property-tax figure of $120,234 for tax year 2026. Those carrying costs sit alongside the asking price for anyone assessing the full expense of owning the estate.Clarkson has not publicly explained why he is selling the house. The available reporting does not establish whether the decision is connected to his basketball career, another property purchase or a personal reason. The listing price also does not guarantee that the home will sell for that amount.Jordan Clarkson's San Antonio roots go back to his childhood Spurs memoriesThe property is in the city where Clarkson attended Karen J. Wagner High School. He grew up watching the Spurs during their championship years, long before he entered the NBA. In June 2026, while preparing to face San Antonio in the NBA Finals with the New York Knicks, Clarkson spoke about the memories he had of the team's title celebrations.“My stepmom worked at the Westin, so I would see the parades through the hotel balconies and stuff. I would sneak around there,” Clarkson said during NBA Finals media availability on June 2, 2026. He recalled that visiting NBA teams stayed at the downtown hotel, giving him opportunities to take pictures with players and ask for autographs. “I was definitely that kid,” he added.Clarkson also recalled how the city came alive during the Spurs' Finals appearances. “Around to see this energy and see how alive the city comes when the Spurs are in the Finals and winning championships. It's a great experience,” he said. The remarks offered a personal look at his connection to San Antonio while he prepared to compete against the franchise he had followed as a child.That hometown history is separate from the real estate decision. Clarkson has not said that his memories of San Antonio influenced the sale, and there is no confirmed explanation for his plans for the house. articles.body:
It didn't take long for Luka Dončić and Yaxel Lendeborg to turn the 2026-27 season chippy.

In the season debut for both the Los Angeles Lakers and Golden State Warriors, the pair barked back and forth in the first half, eventually leading to Lendeborg being hit with a technical foul.

It's safe to say that Luka got the best of the exchange.

There's not backing down, and then there's poking the bear needlessly. Golden State's rookie learned the very important distinction between the two on Wednesday night.

articles.title: ‘Don’t do it rook’ – Warriors rookie’s heated exchange with Luka Doncic has fans buzzing after backfiring
articles.summary: Los Angeles Lakers superstar Luka Doncic sent an emphatic message to Golden State Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg for trash-talking him in the first half of...
articles.body:
Los Angeles Lakers superstar Luka Doncic sent an emphatic message to Golden State Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg for trash-talking him in the first half of their opening-night clash.

Lendeborg is making his NBA debut with the Warriors against the Lakers in a nationally televised game. The 24-year-old tried to show he is fearless by taking on the challenge of guarding Luka Doncic, which led to him trying to trash-talk the six-time All-NBA First Team guard.

After Lendeborg's attempt at trash-talking Doncic, the 27-year-old Slovenian responded in the most emphatic way possible.

Yaxel Lendeborg's trash-talk attempt to Luka Doncic ends in disaster

After Doncic managed to lull Yaxel into fouling him with less than three minutes left in the second quarter, the rookie started jawing at Doncic, with Luka not afraid to respond.

This moment would spark Doncic into scoring nine points over the next two minutes, with the final three points coming with a half-court buzzer-beating three-point heave over Lendeborg.

Fans are already mocking the Warriors rookie for poking the tiger and ensuring that Doncic is motivated to destroy them for the rest of the evening.

"Don't do it, rook," warned one concerned fan .

"Does he not know that talking to Luka Doncic is the worst thing you can do?" said a fan .

"Yaxel's welcome to the league moment," said one fan .

"Yaxel gonna learn the hard way," said another fan .

"Lendeborg really woke Luka up in the 2nd quarter. Bad idea, rook. Real bad idea," mentioned a fan .

Doncic ended the first half with 23 points, six rebounds and four assists as the Lakers hold a 66-52 lead over the Warriors. Lendeborg's first half of NBA basketball has him putting up a respectable five points, two rebounds, two assists and a steal, playing admirable defence on Doncic.

Unfortunately, Doncic has far more offensive counters for Lendeborg and the Warriors' defence than they can game plan for, as Luka got more comfortable on the court as the quarter wore on.

articles.title: Ja Morant shows off 3-point range on 1st bucket with Blazers
articles.summary: Ja Morant put on a new NBA uniform for the first time in his career Wednesday. Fans envisioned the former Memphis Grizzlies star bringing his highlight reel...
articles.body:
Ja Morant put on a new NBA uniform for the first time in his career Wednesday. Fans envisioned the former Memphis Grizzlies star bringing his highlight reel dunks to the Portland Trail Blazers . But instead he showed his three-point range against the Phoenix Suns.

Morant banked this basket from near the Moda Center logo to ignite the crowd.

Morant originally appeared to be ready for a bench role in his Blazers debut. He walked into a place that featured more than franchise legend Damian Lillard . Savvy veterans Jrue Holiday and Scoot Henderson also comprised the backcourt for Portland. Yet this look presented Portland with a possible logjam at the guard spots now that the polarizing Morant was on board.

But head coach Micah Nori made the decision to plug Morant with "Dame Time" on the backend. The chemistry ignited from there between the past NBA All-Stars.

Morant scored six points in his first eight minutes of play on the floor. Lillard made 12 points through his first 12 minutes of action. And Portland exploded to a commanding 45-22 lead early on during the second quarter.

Memphis pulled off the massive trade involving Morant back in June 2026 . Kris Murray and Jerami Grant became a part of the deal that sent both to the Grizzlies in exchange for Morant.

The latter left the franchise averaging 22.4 points per game. But Morant's tenure was marred with controversy. Notably for flashing a handgun in multiple instances including over a live social media video broadcasted via Instagram in May 2023.

Yet now Morant looks like he's taken advantage of his new surroundings early.

articles.title: Rhyne Howard wreaks havoc with 5 steals as Atlanta routs Golden State in Game 3
articles.summary: ATLANTA (AP) — Rhyne Howard has been a ball hawk for Atlanta on the defensive end all season long, leading the WNBA in steals.She's upped her play in the WNB...
articles.body:
ATLANTA (AP) — Rhyne Howard has been a ball hawk for Atlanta on the defensive end all season long, leading the WNBA in steals.

She's upped her play in the WNBA Finals. Howard had five steals on Wednesday night in Atlanta's 97-71 rout of the Golden State Valkyries in Game 3. That came after she had six steals in the Game 2 victory. She's the first player in WNBA history to have consecutive games with five or more steals.

"On the other side you have one of the better scorers (Gabby Williams) in the postseason, so I just needed to make her life hard, take her shots away, take her looks away, get in the passing lanes and making sure that they're not getting anything easy, as opposed to what we're trying to get on the offensive end," said Howard, who averaged 2.3 steals this season.

Howard and the Dream have been locked in defensively the entire series so far. Even in the Game 1 loss they only gave up 68 points. They just didn't force as many turnovers. On Wednesday, Atlanta turned 17 Golden State turnovers into 22 points.

"We're No. 1 in a lot of categories, and that first game we didn't show why," Howard said. "So I think Game 2 and Game 3 today, we showed why we were No. 1 in those categories not only in the postseason, but in the games leading up."

Golden State guard Veronica Burton knows the Valkyries need to do better taking care of the basketball, especially when Howard is around.

"She's long. I think she's deceptively long, and she has good instincts," Burton said. "We've got to take care of the ball more when she's in the gaps."

Howard also had her offense going in the victory with 16 points, four assists and four rebounds. She had 17 points combined in the first two games. The All-Star was more aggressive getting to the basket instead of settling for 3-pointers. Howard had 10 free throw attempts while only attempting two 3-pointers.

articles.title: Enes Kanter Freedom denied entry to WNBA Finals after he refused to sit in a suite
articles.summary: Enes Kanter Freedom has spent months trying to stir up controversy around the WNBA, and he planned to bring that campaign to Game 3 of the WNBA Finals on Wed...
articles.body:
Enes Kanter Freedom has spent months trying to stir up controversy around the WNBA, and he planned to bring that campaign to Game 3 of the WNBA Finals on Wednesday night. But it didn't go the way he wanted.

Kanter Freedom was denied entry to State Farm Arena after he refused to watch the game from a private suite, which the Atlanta Dream and the arena had arranged in response to his own concerns about his safety. Instead, he spent the night posting videos on social media complaining that he couldn't sit in the seats he had purchased.

Over the summer, Kanter Freedom and fellow former NBA player Royce White both announced plans to enter the 2027 WNBA Draft, saying that they identify as women. The goal has been to pressure the league into taking a stand on transgender women.

Last week, WNBA Commissioner Cathy Engelbert told Congress that neither of them is eligible because they are "both men." And Kanter Freedom responded by asking , "IS THE #WNBA TRANSPHOBIC?"

"Apparently, the WNBA still can't define what a WOMAN is, but they're absolutely certain they know what a MAN is! How convenient!" he wrote on X .

Kanter Freedom announced on Saturday that he planned to attend Game 3, saying that he was inspired by Valkyries star Gabby Williams, who has said that she would welcome a transgender teammate.

"Her words gave me so much hope and motivation to come out as a woman and officially declare for the WNBA draft," Kanter Freedom wrote . "I can't wait to watch my favorite player, the woman who inspired me to become who I am today!"

He also took a shot at Dream star Angel Reese, who he said had blocked him on social media.

"I can't wait to take some notes on how to finish a layup after grabbing a rebound," Kanter Freedom wrote.

It was his first WNBA game since August, when he was ejected from a Chicago Sky game and banned from the arena after a heated interaction with Sky guard Natasha Cloud. He has since filed a lawsuit against the Sky over the ban.

Before the game, State Farm Arena released a statement saying that Kanter Freedom had contacted federal, state, and local authorities, as well as the WNBA and the Dream, to express concerns about his safety.

"Following consultations with the WNBA, Dream ownership, State Farm Arena leadership and security officials, we have directed Mr. Freedom to watch tonight's game from a private luxury suite," the arena said, via ESPN . "This arrangement is intended to address his security concerns and help provide a safe and positive experience for him and other guests."

The arena added that the suite would have additional security, and that state police had assigned an officer to him at his request.

But Kanter Freedom wasn't interested. In a video posted to X , he claimed that arena security was "banning us from our purchased seats."

"I guess they have to escort me out of the building," he added.

At halftime, he posted another video showing him being told at the entry gate, "If you come in you have to agree to go to the suite."

"I purchased tickets, right? Just because I purchased tickets, I would like to sit in my seat. That's all I want," Kanter Freedom responded.

An Atlanta police officer then told him that he was "free to go to the city of Atlanta streets," but that "he just can't be here."

A State Farm Arena official said that Kanter Freedom "was offered the suite for his safety and he rejected it."

articles.title: Enes Kanter Freedom says WNBA booted him after he refused private suite
articles.summary: Moments before the Valkyries and the Dream were set to play Game 3 of the WNBA Finals on Wednesday night, former NBA player Enes Kanter Freedom said he was k...
articles.body:
Moments before the Valkyries and the Dream were set to play Game 3 of the WNBA Finals on Wednesday night, former NBA player Enes Kanter Freedom said he was kicked out of State Farm Arena.

Freedom's exit from the stadium came after he declined to stay in a private suite that was provided to him by the Dream as a safety measure.

According to a statement from State Farm Arena , "Enes Kanter Freedom has contacted federal, state and local authorities, the WNBA, the Atlanta Dream and State Farm Arena officials to express concerns about his personal safety during his planned attendance at Game 3 of the WNBA Finals tonight," the statement read. "The safety and security of our guests and team members is our highest priority.

"Following consultations with the WNBA, Dream ownership, State Farm Arena leadership and security officials, we have directed Mr. Freedom to watch tonight's game from a private luxury suite. This arrangement is intended to address his security concerns and help provide a safe and positive experience for him and other guests. The suite will have additional security and will be his designated viewing location for the game. State police have also assigned an officer to Mr. Freedom at his request."

Before the game started, Freedom posted a video of himself on X with the caption that read, "Just talked to director of the @NBA and they are now banning us from our purchased seats."

Freedom went on to write, "Shame on @WNBA. I guess they have to escort me out of the building. Stay tuned."

While the game went on without him, Freedom showed up to the stadium during halftime while wearing a black shirt that read "What Is A Woman?"

Freedom was immediately met by a team official and was told, "If you come in you have to agree to go to the suite."

Freedom told the Dream official, "I purchased tickets, right? Just because I purchased tickets, I would like to sit at my seat."

As Freedom continued to try and negotiate his way into the stadium, an Atlanta police officer told him, "We have to get off State Farm property. You're free to go to the city of Atlanta streets. That's another private establishment over there. He's free to go to there. He just can't be here."

Freedom was then seen exiting the arena and said, "They kicked me out of the game for supporting women. They're not letting me in the arena for protecting women and supporting women. Shame on the NBA. Shame on the WNBA."

On Monday, Freedom posted a video on X announcing his intentions to attend Game 3 of the WNBA Finals.

Freedom said he was looking forward to seeing Valkyries star, Gabby Williams , as he wrote, "this all started with an interview featuring Gabby Williams of the Golden State @Valkyries, when she said, 'I have no problem with trans athletes playing on my team or against my team.'"

Freedom has been in the controversial limelight as of late, when he announced over the summer that he was planning to enter the WNBA Draft as a transgender athlete .

articles.title: Charles Barkley takes a ‘dangerous’ Kash Patel dig at Shaquille O’Neal
articles.summary: Shaquille O’Neal’s ties to the FBI led to a hilarious shot from Charles Barkley as Inside the NBA returned to the delight of NBA fans everywhere. The NBA sea...
articles.body:
Shaquille O'Neal's ties to the FBI led to a hilarious shot from Charles Barkley as Inside the NBA returned to the delight of NBA fans everywhere.

The NBA season is officially back, and while the basketball aspect of that is very exciting, fans are happy about more than just that. Inside the NBA with Ernie Johnson, Kenny Smith, Charles Barkley, and Shaquille O'Neal is back too, and they're already going viral.

Shaq is known for being someone who has varied interests. His post-NBA career involves everything from receiving honorary doctorates, to becoming a DJ and selling out concerts. O'Neal has also had a history of being involved with law enforcement. Barkley brought that up on their first show of the season.

Charles Barkley hilariously asked whether he should 'stand close' to Shaquille O'Neal because of Kash Patel

FBI Director Kash Patel has dealt with several issues during his tenure at the head of the law enforcement agency. One of the lighter moments recently has been when he named the Los Angeles Lakers legend an honorary FBI Special Agent in September.

At that time, Shaq even joked that his Inside the NBA co-host Barkley should be arrested. While they were covering the Miami Heat and Minnesota Timberwolves game, Chuck finally responded.

"Should we be standing this close to Shaq? He's been hanging out with Kash Patel. That's dangerous," Barkley said, leading to laughter from all his co-hosts. Ernie Johnson added, "Ooh! Ooh! Oh, I didn't know you were going there. But I should have known you would."

Having the NBA legends back is likely to lead to a lot more moments that will crack fans up. Nothing is off limits when it comes to Barkley, and his tongue-in-cheek comments to Shaq are what make the show what it is.

articles.title: Haliburton makes an emotional return from his injury and leads the Pacers to an opening-night win
articles.summary: NEW ORLEANS (AP) — Tyrese Haliburton needed the towel draped around his neck to dry the tears streaming down his cheeks.More than 16 months after rupturing h...
articles.body:
NEW ORLEANS (AP) — Tyrese Haliburton needed the towel draped around his neck to dry the tears streaming down his cheeks.

More than 16 months after rupturing his right Achilles tendon, the Indiana Pacers two-time All-Star guard had come back Wednesday night and controlled his team's season opener, removing any doubts he might have had about his physical and emotional stamina.

"It feels like it just took forever to get here," Haliburton said after scoring 23 points, including 13 in the final quarter, and adding 12 assists as the Pacers beat the New Orleans Pelicans 123-120 . "You know, it's been, what 16, 17 months, but I just really appreciate being here."

Haliburton tore his Achilles during Game 7 of the NBA Finals against Oklahoma City in June 2025 and missed the entire 2025-26 season. He averaged 18.6 points and 9.2 assists, shooting 47.3% from the field and 38.8% from 3-point range in his last full season.

He made three 3-pointers in just seven minutes in that Game 7 before his injury.

All that was a distant memory as he stepped on the court Wednesday in his first real action since the injury. The tears flowed when he did a courtside interview with Jeremiah Johnson, the sideline reporter for the Pacers' postgame show.

"I had moments in private, especially early, when it was hard," Haliburton said. "I thought that this moment would just feel like super emotional for me. I didn't think I was going to cry. It hit me kind of there when talking to Jeremiah, and you know, seeing all those like Pacers fans in the arena. We haven't won here in five years or whatever, and to see all those Pacers fans here in New Orleans for this means a lot to me and this organization. I'm back doing what I love. I'm really happy to be back on the floor."

With the game tied at 116, Haliburton drove past Trey Murphy for a layup, and the next time downcourt, he did the same thing to the Pelicans' defensive specialist, Herb Jones, for a layup and three-point play.

That gave the Pacers the lead for good. Haliburton said he flashed back to the painful, baby steps in his recovery.

"It's just an appreciation," he said. "You know, perspective is everything. As the game was going on, I was struggling a little bit … just kind of tired and just not playing well. We weren't playing well. I think I was kind of sitting there in that moment, and I think what got me going again was … I just kind of took a step back when I was on the floor, and I was just like, 'Man, I'm back playing, I'm back here.' And I just want to live in the moment as much as I can.

"I think we all can relate to that in life as we get older. I'm obviously only 26 years old, but it's a new perspective that I found, and I'm just really appreciative to be playing."

Haliburton hit the floor hard on one collision with Zion Williamson, but he bounced right back up.

"The thing that's made me feel most like normal is falling and our whole team not panicking," Haliburton said. "I think that's made me feel the most normal. I think I was just on the ground (trying) to breathe a little bit. I'm tired as hell. You can do all the sprinting, track workouts, hard workouts you want. It's nothing like game shape. So it'll come with time, and yeah, that baptism by fire is good."

Packers coach Rick Carlisle said he was amazed Haliburton played nearly 34 minutes, and he loved how his point guard controlled the fourth quarter.

"Ty came back in and he had enough in the tank, and it was spectacular," Carlisle said.

articles.title: Rockets predicted to trade for Mavericks' $118M veteran NBA champion to reunite with Kevin Durant
articles.summary: The Houston Rockets might just make a power move to give themselves a shot at an NBA championship. In this proposed deal, they get one of the best to ever do...
articles.body:
The Dallas Mavericks are going to be a team to watch early in the season, but not for the reason many might think. It isn't about whether Dallas wins or loses; it's about the direction the franchise decides to take.

Kyrie Irving has been involved in trade speculation all summer, and that is likely to continue. However, Irving has been clear that he wants to stay with the Mavericks.

"I'm not gonna shy away from saying it's been a little chaotic at times, inside the locker room as well as outside…I'm in love with this place just because of how welcoming it was, not just from the franchise aspect but also the fans, lot of support around the city…We're building something…Having that championship mindset that whatever we face we can deal with," Irving said.

If the team reaches a point where it is struggling and Irving wants out, there is a belief that the Mavericks would grant his request.

"Masai also has a really good relationship as you mentioned with Kyrie Irving. I think it's the kind of relationship where if Kyrie says, hey, Masai, like, this isn't for me, I think they could work together to get something done. I don't think would be something ugly. I think there would be interest in Kyrie if he's as healthy as he looks," NBA insider Marc Spears said.

If a trade does come into the picture, CBS Sports' Sam Quinn believes Irving could be traded to the Houston Rockets for a reunion with Kevin Durant.

"He's 34 and his team's franchise player is 19. Timeline issues don't need to be deal-breakers, but the Mavericks don't control their own first-round pick again until 2031. They have to find longer-term assets where they can, and Irving is their most desirable trade piece. How does a reunion with Kevin Durant in Houston sound," Quinn wrote.

The duo still believe they should have won an NBA Finals during their time with the Brooklyn Nets , but that never happened. Now, they could have another opportunity to make a run in the Western Conference.

Irving is in the final year of his $118 million contract with the Mavericks . With Dallas in need of valuable draft capital, trading Irving could make sense if the franchise decides to move in a different direction.

articles.title: Damian Lillard drops 25 points in Trail Blazers return, leads historic 41-point rout over Suns in season opener
articles.summary: The Trail Blazers opened Wednesday night with a 21-0 run, the largest run to open a contest anywhere in the league over the past 25 years.
articles.body:
It may be a long season for Devin Booker and the Phoenix Suns.

They opened the 2026-27 campaign in perhaps the worst possible way on Wednesday night at the Moda Center, and couldn't do anything to slow down Damian Lillard in his official return to the floor for the Trail Blazers. Portland, after a historic opening half, rolled to a blowout 124-83 win over the Suns to kick off the season.

Lillard dropped 25 points and went 6 of 10 from behind the arc in his official return to Portland. The longtime former Trail Blazers star signed a three-year deal to return to the franchise, but he missed all of last season recovering from an Achilles injury he suffered when he was with the Milwaukee Bucks.

It was bad for Phoenix from the jump, too. The Trail Blazers opened the game on a 21-0 run, which marked the largest run to start a game anywhere in the league over the past 25 seasons, according to OptaStats . Both Booker and new Trail Blazers star Ja Morant got into it briefly on the floor. Both guys were separated pretty quickly, but they each received a technical foul.

It didn't get any better, either. The Trail Blazers took a 43-12 lead by the end of the first quarter, and held the Suns to just 4-of-20 shooting in the opening period. They made only a single shot through the first nine minutes, too.

Lillard made the most of his return, too. He dropped 12 points in the opening quarter and hit a trio of 3-pointers, including one from the Moda Center logo.

The second quarter was better for Phoenix, though not by much. The Trail Blazers ended up taking a 33-point lead into the break, which marked the largest halftime lead of a season-opener in franchise history.

Lillard had 17 of his 25 points at halftime. Booker, with 10, was the only Suns player in double figures entering the locker room.

The Trail Blazers didn't let up, either. They pushed their lead to 41 points by the end of the third, thanks in part to a huge step-back 3-pointer from Lillard in the final minute of the period. It was his sixth 3-pointer of the night.

By then, Portland simply held on the rest of the way to grab the 41-point win. It marked the team's first opening-night win since 2022, and the third-largest win to open a season in team history.

Booker led the Suns with 23 points while shooting 7 of 13 from the field. Dillon Brooks and Jalen Green each added 10 points, and were the only other Suns players to hit double figures.

Deni Avdija added 18 points and 10 rebounds to go with Lillard's 25-point outing. Toumani Camara also had 18 points, and Morant — who was dealt to the Trail Blazers by the Grizzlies earlier this offseason — finished with 14 points and eight assists.

While he's nearing the end of his career, Lillard is clearly back to full strength and ready for his second run in Portland.

articles.title: UC Bearcats legend captures Bob Huggins' legacy perfectly | Williams
articles.summary: Williams: It's reflection time about the coaching greatness of Bob Huggins, who's in declining health. And no one epitomized that more than Steve Logan.
articles.body:
When word began circulating behind the scenes about Bob Huggins' declining health this week, I immediately thought of one guy.

No one represented Huggins' greatness as a basketball coach more than the former University of Cincinnati All-American guard.

Huggins took an underrated and undersized kid raised by his grandmother in inner-city Cleveland and made him great. Huggins was brutally hard on Logan during his early days at UC in the late 1990s, even called him a "fat kid" to try to motivate the pudgy point guard.

In return, Logan responded by developing into a four-year starter, team leader and star on some of the best teams of Huggins' hall-of-fame career from 1998-2002. Logan is one of three former Bearcats greats, along with Nick Van Exel and Kenyon Martin, scheduled to speak at Huggins' induction ceremony into UC's James P. Kelly Athletics Hall of Fame on Oct. 23.

Huggins was loyal to Logan. Huggins loved Logan. And vice versa. They remain close to this day, an unbreakable bond between coach and player, even as Huggins copes with a progressive cognitive condition, which became publicly known on Oct. 21.

Four years ago, Huggins returned to Cincinnati for a reunion to celebrate the 1992 Final Four team. Huggins and Logan had a moment to speak while the coach and a bunch of former players were at dinner that weekend. It's a conversation Logan told me he'll never forget.

"He said, 'Lo, I've coached a ton of guys. I've coached a lot of guys who've gone onto the NBA. But I can count on one hand how many guys mastered me – and you are one of those guys,' " Logan said on Wednesday. "I still get goosebumps thinking about him telling me that."

Logan added: "He's a lot of things in one – father figure, mentor. I want people to know that he had a big, loving side to him."

Huggins, 73, will be celebrated this weekend for returning UC basketball back to national relevance during his 16 seasons in Cincinnati. The hall of fame plaques – Huggins has one in the Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame – highlight the wins and NCAA Tournament success. But it's guys like Steve Logan who epitomize the type of coach Huggins was. He recruited a lot of guys who weren't superstars coming out of high school, was tough on them and then remained loyal for a lifetime to the guys who bought into his system.

Bob Huggins has 'progressive cognitive condition.' See photos of coach

Logan led Lakewood St. Edward to a state championship as a senior in 1998. I covered him in the state tournament that year. Logan was certainly recruited by some big programs. But at 5-foot-11 with chubby cheeks and a muffin top, Logan was far from a surefire college star.

"I had a lot of talent, but I didn't know how to work," Logan said. "When I first got (to UC), he was calling me the 'little fat kid from Cleveland.' I said, 'I don't really like that.' He didn't care. He said, 'Until you get in shape, that's what I'm going to call you.' "

Logan added: "That's why I wanted to go play for him. It's rough. It's tough. He used that to motivate me. He's a genius."

Kenyon Martin, another guy who "mastered" Huggins, left UC as the national player of the year after Logan's sophomore season. Logan was fully bought into Huggins' system by then, in great shape and had earned the coach's trust to take over as team leader. And once you've earned Huggins' respect, he'd let players give it back to him sometimes. He and Logan could butt heads and neither took it personal.

Huggins would tell beat reporters about Logan: "He gives hope to fat people."

"I said, 'What are going to call me now?' " Logan said. "He couldn't call me 'fat' anymore. That's when he started calling me 'Lo.' "

Logan ranks second all-time in scoring at UC, sandwiched between Oscar Robertson and Huggins-era star Danny Fortson on the list. Logan got there on sheer will, following Huggins' blueprint of constantly being in the gym, studying film and playing hurt at times.

Huggins came to love Logan so much that the coach let the player leave the team for a few days during the 2001 NCAA Tournament. Logan's grandmother was sick and near death when UC was in Southern California preparing to play in the Sweet Sixteen. Not many coaches would do that, a testament to the special relationship Huggins and Logan had built.

"He allowed me to take the trip to talk to her, to hug her," Logan told former Enquirer reporter Bill Koch for his 2022 book titled "Huggs." "I'm forever grateful to him for doing that."

How bought into Huggins' system was Logan?

Logan plans to share a story during Huggins' induction ceremony about when he played with a severe ankle sprain in the championship game of the 2000 Puerto Rico Holiday Classic. Logan had suffered the injury in the second game of the tournament.

"It was bad," Logan said. "They carried me off the floor and took me to the emergency room. The doctor diagnosed me with a high ankle sprain, gave me crutches and said I'd be out 3-5 weeks. We're back at the hotel. I'm sobbing. Huggs comes to my room. He looked at me and said, 'Lo, the doctors don't know what they're talking about. We need you to play tomorrow.' "

"Tomorrow?" Logan responded to his coach.

Huggins said: Team trainer Jayd Grossman "is going to rub your ankle down all night and in the morning you're going to feel better and we're going to win this championship."

"And it happened just like that," said Logan, who also shared that story in Koch's book.

Logan took over that game against 17th-ranked Alabama, scoring 9 of his 13 points during an 11-1 second-half run to lead UC to a 77-74 overtime win.

"That's the mental toughness that rubbed off on his players," Logan said. "It was him saying, 'I just need you to give me what you have in the championship game.' He taught you life lessons about always going to work, even when you're hurting and tired. He knew how to get the best out of you."

articles.title: Lillard returns with 25 points, Morant debuts and the Blazers rout the Suns 124-83
articles.summary: (AP) — Damian Lillard scored 25 points in his first regular-season game since rejoining the Trail Blazers, leading Portland to a 124-83 season-opening rout o...
articles.body:
PORTLAND, Ore. (AP) — Damian Lillard scored 25 points in his first regular-season game since rejoining the Trail Blazers, leading Portland to a 124-83 season-opening rout of the Phoenix Suns on Wednesday night.

Offseason addition Ja Morant had 14 points and eight assists for the Blazers, who jumped out to a 21-0 lead and led by as many as 52 points. Toumani Camara added 18 points.

Devin Booker, embarking on his 12th NBA season with the Suns, had 23 points.

Lillard spent his first 11 NBA seasons with the Blazers before playing two seasons with the Milwaukee Bucks. He rejoined the Blazers in the summer of 2025, but spent last season rehabbing from a torn Achilles tendon.

Lillard joins a Blazers team that snapped a five-year postseason drought last season. But Tiago Splitter, who took over as coach after Chauncey Billups' arrest in an alleged gambling scheme, left for the Chicago Bulls and the Blazers hired Micah Nori , an assistant with the Timberwolves.

The Blazers also traded away Jerami Grant and Kris Murray to the Memphis Grizzlies in exchange for Morant.

The Blazers went ahead 21-0 behind 3-pointers from Lillard, Morant, Deni Avdija and Donovan Clingan. The Suns' first points came off free throws with 5:54 left in the first quarter.

Lillard made back-to-back 3-pointers to extend the lead to 38-8 and Portland had a 72-39 advantage at halftime. He finished with six 3s.

The Suns hit just 36% from the field for the game and were just 6 of 31 on 3-point attempts.

Nori pulled the Blazers' starters early in the final quarter.

Avdija was a game-time decision for the Blazers with a right ankle injury but started. Avdija, last season's surprising breakout player with 24.2 points per game, had 18 points and 10 rebounds.

The Suns host the Golden State Warriors on Saturday.

The Blazers visit the Sacramento Kings on Friday.

articles.title: Luka Dončić-led Lakers begin post-LeBron James era with blowout win over Warriors
articles.summary: Luka Dončić and Walker Kessler both had big games.
articles.body:
For the first time since 2017, the Los Angeles Lakers began their season without LeBron James on the roster. But they still have Luka Dončić.

That was more than enough for their season opener on Wednesday, a 127-105 home win over the short-handed Golden State Warriors.

Dončić certainly looked eager to define this Lakers era, posting 28 points on 7-of-18 shooting, 8 rebounds, 7 assists and 3 steals. He spent much of the game matched up against Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg and appeared to take the assignment personally. He repeatedly went after the No. 12 pick of the 2026 NBA Draft and let him know about it after the play.

That included on a half-court shot to end the first half, pointing at Lendeborg after the buzzer.

That's something of a "Welcome to the NBA" moment for Lendeborg, who won an NCAA championship and All-American honors last season at Michigan.

So Dončić appears ready to keep doing his thing without James. As for the other Lakers, trade acquisition Walker Kessler had a big Lakers debut with 26 points on 12-of-12 shooting. His 10 dunks were the most by a Laker in a single game since a big man by the name of Shaquille O'Neal in 2003.

Dončić assisted on five of those dunks, forming the kind of two-man game when the Lakers had in mind when they gave the big man a four-year, $130 million sign-and-trade deal .

The new-look defense made life tough for the Warriors, who are without Jimmy Butler, Kristaps Porziņģis and Moses Moody to open the season. Stephen Curry led the group with 23 points, but Golden State shot only 27 of 70 as a team before emptying out its bench at the start of the fourth quarter.

The sour note for the night was a painful-looking injury for Jake LaRavia, a returnee expected to get rotation minutes this season. He appeared to roll his ankle on a drive during garbage time.

It was a transformative season overall for the Lakers. Among the nine Lakers players to see pre-garbage-time minutes on Wednesday only three members were part of the Lakers last season: Dončić, Austin Reaves and LaRavia.

James is gone. Marcus Smart is gone. Rui Hachimura is gone. DeAndre Ayton, Luke Kennard and Jaxson Hayes are all gone. The Lakers responded by bringing in the likes of Kessler, Matisse Thybulle and Ziaire Williams, who all started against the Warriors, plus Quentin Grimes, Sandro Mamukelashvili and Kevon Looney, who came off the bench.

There aren't many places bullish on the idea of this group doing what the James-led group couldn't in his last few years in Los Angeles, but the transformation was likely inevitable once Dončić came to town. This is now a team built entirely around the 27-year-old, with the ability to try building for beyond this season.

Wednesday at least represents a good start in that regard.
